- $OP=4|p|$

Similarly:

- $PR=4|q|$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PR} \\  & =4p+4q.\end{aligned}

Consequently, $r=\lambda p+\mu q=4p+4q.$

Since $p∦q,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =4$ and $\mu =4$

In $△OMR$ shown above, we have:

- $OM=\frac{11}{4}|q|$

- $\overset{\to }{OM}$ has the opposite direction to $q$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OM}=-\frac{11}{4}q.$

Similarly:

- $MR=\frac{11}{4}|p|$

- $\overset{\to }{MR}$ and $p$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{MR}=\frac{11}{4}p.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\overset{\to }{OM}+\overset{\to }{MR} \\  & =-\frac{11}{4}q+\frac{11}{4}p \\  & =\frac{11}{4}p-\frac{11}{4}q.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $r=\lambda p+\mu q=\frac{11}{4}p-\frac{11}{4}q.$

Since $p∦q,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =\frac{11}{4}$ and $\mu =-\frac{11}{4}$
